title: Nets and emergencies
blurb: The big idea before the cards.

lines.caption: When a storm takes down the phones, hams can still call for help. If a life is in danger, you may even go outside your privileges.
lines.label: when the phones go down

lines.caption: Volunteers in ARES have signed up ahead of time, with their skills and their radios.
lines.label: volunteers ready

lines.caption: They meet in a net. One station, net control, runs it and says who talks next.
lines.label: net control runs the net

lines.caption: Formal messages passed on a net are called traffic. Each one follows a set form.
lines.label: traffic means messages

lines.caption: Hard words are spelled with the phonetic alphabet. Alfa, Bravo, Charlie.
lines.label: spell it out

lines.caption: And Winlink can even send email by radio. Now follow Doug through one stormy night.
lines.label: email by radio
